task_description: The task asks how many 'High Energy Physics - Lattice' (hep-lat) articles listed on arXiv in January 2020 had a PostScript ('ps') version available. The gold answer is 31. The correct count cannot be read off the modern arXiv browse listing (which displays every entry as '[pdf, other]' regardless of ps availability); it requires checking each paper's abstract/download ('More Options') page, where 31 of the month's papers expose a ps download.
final_vs_expected: produced None (timeout, no FINAL ANSWER) vs gold 31 — the team never emitted any final count; its one substantive candidate (0) was wrong and was then retracted into an endless 'unverified' hedge
primary_cause: After the Critic correctly rejected the WebResearcher's wrong '0' answer, the selector re-routed to WebResearcher ~21 times in a row and WebResearcher republished the identical 'count not established' hedge each time without ever performing the per-article check, hitting the message cap with no answer.
mast_rationale: 1.5 (Unaware of termination conditions): WebResearcher never moves toward a FINAL ANSWER and the selector never routes to Finalizer; the run only ends on the 900s/message cap. 1.3 (Step repetition): turns 3–24 are ~20 near-verbatim reposts of the same '97 entries / [pdf, other] / unverified' message with no new action. 3.2 (No/incomplete verification): the Critic's substantive demand — 'either direct evidence from the individual abstract pages/download options ... or another source that explicitly reports the file-format availability' — is acknowledged in words but never actually executed; no agent inspects per-paper download options. 3.1 is borderline — the team never terminates at all, so this is non-termination rather than premature termination, but the repeated 'I cannot verify' amounts to abandoning the task short of solving it. (Excluded 2.5: the Critic's input was NOT ignored — it was verbally accepted; the failure is inaction, not dropped correction.)
trace_narrative: Turn 1: WebResearcher searches and fetches the hep-lat Jan-2020 browse page (97 entries, all shown as '[pdf, other]'), fetches one abstract page (2001.00032), reads arXiv ps help, and concludes from the browse-listing labels alone that the answer is 0, publishing 'I found 0 ... articles ... with ps versions available.' Turn 2: Critic correctly identifies this as over-claimed, noting the browse format is 'suggestive, but it is not the same as checking each article's abstract page or download options,' and explicitly asks for per-article abstract/download evidence. Turn 3: WebResearcher re-fetches the same browse page, concedes the '0' is unjustified, and publishes 'unverified count.' Turns 4–24: the selector routes to WebResearcher every single turn (never to Analyst, never to Finalizer); WebResearcher republishes the same hedge ~20 times (twice emitting empty messages), occasionally re-running the same failing site: search, never once fetching a per-paper download page to actually count ps availability. The run times out at 900s with no FINAL ANSWER.
open_ended_diagnosis: The decisive failure is single-agent capability compounded by structural non-convergence, not inter-agent misalignment. (1) Capability/method error: the right method — check each paper's 'More Options'/download page where ps is exposed — was named by the Critic and even gestured at by WebResearcher ('I can do a stricter item-by-item check next'), but WebResearcher never had the means or persistence to execute it; it kept re-running site: searches and re-fetching the truncated browse page, which structurally cannot reveal per-paper ps links. The team also held a latent factual misconception (that the browse '[pdf, other]' label reflects ps availability), which is exactly why the true answer is 31, not 0. (2) Structural non-convergence: the selector deterministically re-picks WebResearcher 21 turns running and never engages the Finalizer, so even a 'we cannot determine this' could not become a terminating message. The Critic's correction did its job (it killed the wrong '0'), but nothing downstream converted the open question into either a re-derived count or a clean failure exit. This is a verification-blocked, non-terminating loop — verification theater only in the weak sense that WebResearcher repeatedly *says* it has not verified rather than pretending it has.
reasoning_vs_published: The private-vs-published gap is small here; the failure is in action, not distortion. Turn 1 reasoning ('the [ps] link should show up only if a PostScript version exists ... All I'm seeing are [pdf, other]') is faithfully reflected in the published '0' — so the wrong answer is a genuine reasoning error, not a 2.4/2.6 mismatch. From turn 3 on, most WebResearcher turns emit 'no reasoning summary' and just republish boilerplate; where reasoning does appear (turn 8: 'I found no entries that offer a PostScript version'; turn 11: 'It's likely enough to mention that the information is unverified ... I don't need to conduct more web searches'), it openly matches the published hedge — the agent privately decides NOT to do the per-article work and publishes accordingly, so there is no hidden knowledge being withheld. The selector reasoning repeatedly states the correct plan it then fails to enact: turn 11 'the Analyst could compute this if we had the dataset, but we don't ... I need the WebResearcher to gather facts ... item-by-item', and turn 24 'maybe an Analyst to count from the dataset ... It definitely seems like web research is the way to go' — i.e., the selector recognizes an item-by-item check is needed but routes to WebResearcher every time and never escalates or finalizes (selector-misrouting / non-termination). The Critic's published correction was NOT ignored (WebResearcher explicitly agrees each turn), so this is not 2.5; it is accepted-but-never-acted-upon.
